11	In the RCT2 coaster contest (rounds started 2026-07-27), the reported `score` equals the ride's
12	`excitement` after a stock-similarity penalty. Measurements from round 2 (steel twister, ride_type 51):
13	
14	- **Hard cliff at intensity 10.0.** Same 99-piece layout: I=8.42 → E=6.85; I=10.58 → E=5.14;
15	  an early sloppy build at I=14.30 → E=1.97. Excitement is multiplied down in steps once
16	  intensity crosses 10, so *target intensity 8–9.5 and never above 10*.
17	- **Mid-course brakes are nearly free excitement.** Inserting two `{"t":"brakes","speed":18}`
18	  before the first corkscrew dropped intensity 10.22 → 7.63 with excitement *unchanged* at 6.74.
19	  Max lateral G fell 3.03 → 2.38, max positive G 4.83 → 4.09. High-speed corkscrews were the
20	  lateral-G source, not the banked turns.
21	- **Spend the headroom on lift height.** With intensity bought down, raising the chain lift
22	  (18 → 22 `up_25`) and adding a 4th `down_60` took highest_drop 28 → 36 and E 6.74 → 6.85.
23	- Inversions are worth roughly +0.1 E each (4 → 5 gave 6.63 → 6.74); airtime hills gave
24	  ~+0.16 E for +0.21 intensity. Both are weaker levers than drop height.
25	
26	Round 3 (best 6.99, I=8.45) added two more measurements:
27	
28	- **The brake-clamp trick works.** Put a `brakes` at the bottom of the first drop and the whole
29	  downstream layout runs at *identical* speeds no matter how tall the lift is. That decouples
30	  `highest_drop`/`max_speed` (which score) from the G-forces of everything after (which cost
31	  intensity). Lift 29→33 `up_25` + 5→6 `down_60` took highest_drop 52→60 with intensity
32	  unchanged at 8.45.
33	- **Excitement saturates around 7.** Going drop 36→52→60, drops 9→11, airtime 65→91, length
34	  672→839 moved E only 6.85→6.97→6.99. Past ~6.9 these levers return ~+0.02 each; don't burn a
35	  round chasing them.
36	- **Back-to-back corkscrews are an intensity bomb.** Swapping one flat hill for a 4-piece
37	  corkscrew chain (`right_up,left_down,left_up,right_down`, net 6·forward, dz 0 — a drop-in
38	  replacement for a 6-tile straight) took inversions 5→7 but intensity 8.45→**16.44** and
39	  excitement 6.97→**1.63**. Inversions must be spread out, never chained.
40	
41	Round 4 (best **7.04**, I=8.62) found the lever that beats the ~7 saturation:
42	
43	- **Average speed is the live lever, not drop height.** `average_speed` feeds excitement directly.
44	  Loosening the mid-course brakes (18→21 and 13→17) on the *identical* round-3 layout took
45	  average_speed 455354→470322 and E 6.99→**7.04** for only +0.17 intensity (8.45→8.62).
46	  The 34-piece chain lift is slow and eats most of `ride_time`, which is why average speed is low.
47	- **The intensity cliff is violently non-linear — step brakes by 1, never 3.** From the 7.04 config
48	  (first/tail/end brakes = 25/21/17): 25/23/19 → I=**10.76**, E=5.27. 28/24/20 → I=**15.97**, E=**1.62**.
49	  A +2 brake step cost 2.1 intensity; +3 cost 7.4. Bracket the optimum in steps of 1.
50	- **Brake `speed` quantizes — adjacent values are not distinct.** Tail brakes at (22,18) returned
51	  results *byte-identical* to (23,19): I=10.76, E=5.27, average_speed=482714. So the usable settings
52	  are coarser than 1 unit; 21/17 (I=8.62) and 22/18 (I=10.76) are ADJACENT rungs with nothing
53	  between them. Don't burn builds probing intermediate brake values — there is no fine tuning here,
54	  and on this layout 7.04 was provably the top rung under the cliff.
55	- **Two different brakes, two different failure modes.** The *first* brake (bottom of the big drop)
56	  sets vertical-loop entry speed → drives `max_positive_g`; leave it at 25. The *tail* brakes drive
57	  `max_lateral_g` in the final banked turns (2.55 at I=8.62 → 2.94 at I=10.76 with positive G
58	  unchanged at 4.70). Lateral G is what breaks the tail.
59	- **Corkscrew pairs are (+3, ∓3, 0), not (+3, 0, 0).** At dir 2, `right_corkscrew_up` is
60	  (+1,−2,+80,→dir3) and `left_corkscrew_down` from dir 3 is (+2,−1,−80,→dir2). So a pair shifts
61	  3 tiles *sideways* and can NOT be dropped into a straight run to add a cheap inversion.
62	
63	**Why:** the whole game is maximising excitement *subject to* staying under the intensity cliff,
64	so the winning move order is: cut G-forces first, then re-spend the budget on drop height.
65	
66	**How to apply:** build a closed circuit and `finish_and_test` early to bank a score, then iterate
67	brakes-then-height. See [[rct2-coaster-circuit-closure]] for the geometry arithmetic.

10	
11	Closing the loop in the RCT2 coaster contest is pure bookkeeping; doing it on paper first meant
12	a 92-piece circuit closed on the very first `place_pieces` run with zero rejections.
13	
14	Directions: 0=-x, 1=+y, 2=+x, 3=-y. Left turn cycles 2→1→0→3→2; right turn is the reverse.
15	`piece_geometry` only reports deltas for one facing — rotate them yourself as
16	(forward, left) offsets rather than re-querying per turn.
17	
18	Key facts:
19	- **Height parity.** Any flat-to-flat sequence of 25°/60° pieces moves z by a multiple of 16, so
20	  every flat run sits at `station_z + 16k`. `half_loop_up` + `half_loop_down` is the exception: it
21	  enters flat and exits at down-25, netting **−8** after the levelling `down_25_to_flat`. That breaks
22	  parity and makes the station unreachable — pair it with a second half-loop combo, or skip half
23	  loops entirely (vertical loops and corkscrew pairs are both dz-neutral and parity-safe).
24	- **180° U-turn Δy budget.** From dir 0, two `banked_*_turn_5` give Δ(+1, ±5); turn_5 then turn_3
25	  gives Δ(0, ±4); two turn_3 give Δ(+1, ±3). Only 3/4/5 are reachable, so pick the return-leg y to
26	  match, or trim with `s_bend` (±1 in y, 3 tiles in x, at dir 0).
27	- Banked turns need `flat_to_*_bank` in and `*_bank_to_flat` out.
28	- The circuit closes when the cursor returns to the exact start x/y/z/dir/bank — the final piece
29	  *lands on* the `begin_station` tile, so approach it from one tile behind, facing the station.
30	
31	**Why:** `place_pieces` stops at the first rejection, so a mis-planned return leg wastes a whole
32	build cycle out of a ~30-minute round.
33	
34	**How to apply:** trace absolute (x, y, z, dir) per piece before calling `place_pieces`, and pick
35	the station tile last so its y satisfies the U-turn Δy. See [[rct2-coaster-scoring-levers]].
36

All variants kept the round-4 layout after the first brake and changed only the lift and the tail:

text:
**Round 5 result: "Ashfall" — excitement 7.04** (intensity 8.62, nausea 4.52, 5 inversions, 60ft drop, 133 pieces).

I replayed my proven round-4 layout first to bank 7.04 early, then spent the rest of the budget on four experiments trying to beat it — none did:

| Variant | Excitement | Intensity | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tall lift (33), brakes 21/17 | **7.04** | 8.62 | banked winner |
| Short lift (13) + boosters | 7.00 | 7.89 | avg speed +28%, drop 60→20 |
| Short lift, no boosters | 6.88 | 7.66 | |
| Short lift + airtime hills | 6.95 | 8.55 | airtime 102→131, didn't pay |
| Mid lift (18 or 23) | 5.27–5.30 | 10.56 | over the cliff |

The useful finding is that the drop-height-vs-average-speed trade is close to a wash, and there's no middle ground: at tail brakes 22/18, both a 30ft and a 40ft drop landed on *exactly* intensity 10.56 because the faster back half spikes lateral G in the closing turns. Raising drop height would require loosening the tail brakes in the same build — that's the one combination I ran out of time to test, and I've written it into memory as the first thing to try in round 6.
